title: R-NES
desc: R-NES is a fully functioning emulator built entirely in Rust for the Nintendo Entertainment System, a gaming console from 1983. The emulator supports 2 mapper types, all 151 offical instructions and syncs cpu/ppu interactions to the clock cycle.

title: LCD Driver
desc: Crafted a Linux kernel module for the 1602A LCD, handling GPIO, initialization, and character device access. Learned instructions, timing requirements, and register control from a datasheet for real-time display updates. Implemented a Python wrapper for the driver, exposing a concise API for scripting and rapid prototyping.

title: Digital Reverb
desc: Developed a NES emulator in Rust, covering 151 CPU instructions, interrupt handling, and 110+ test cases. Built proficiency in Rust lifetimes, closures, and borrow checking through low-level systems modeling. Reverse-engineered NES memory-mapped I/O, including PPU register mirroring and cartridge mappers.

title: UF My Music
desc: Produced a TCP application layer protocol for syncing music files between server/clients. Utilized the OpenSSL library to hash files, ensuring 100% accurate duplicate song file detection. Leveraged multi-threading and semaphores to allow multiple clients to interact with the server simultaneously.

title: Study Sesh
desc: Established a full stack web-app in 22 hours, providing UF students a tool to locate study partners. Made with React, Django RESTful API, and a MongoDB database of 6,000+ scraped UF course entries. Implemented Auth0 for JWT authentication, using a three-way token system to enhance endpoint protection.
